title: Universal openness of Spec(B) over Spec(A) tested on one explicit principal open for a finite generating set

standard_prerequisites.name: Explicit prerequisite boundary
standard_prerequisites.reference: Scheme morphisms, base change, principal opens as a basis; no cited result replaces the retained argument
standard_prerequisites.use: Base change of morphisms of schemes, the fact that principal opens D(g) form a basis of the topology, polynomial algebras and the cartesian square Spec(B[x_1..x_n]) / Spec(A[x_1..x_n]) against Spec(B') / Spec(A'). All are standard; the reduction itself is retained.

core_obligations: Show the if-direction by reducing an arbitrary base change A -> A' and an arbitrary principal open D(g) of Spec(A' tensor_A B) to the single test element h = sum x_i b_i, using that the displayed square of spectra is cartesian.
Identify the image of D(g) under the base change with the inverse image of the given open image of D(h), so openness transfers from the single test case.

proof_roadmap.step: Dispose of the only-if direction, then reduce the converse to testing the images of principal opens after an arbitrary base change A -> A'.

spans.label: reduction to principal opens after base change

proof_roadmap.step: Write g = sum a'_i tensor b_i, build the A-algebra map A[x_1..x_n] -> A' sending x_i to a'_i and h to g, and conclude via the cartesian square that the image of D(g) is an inverse image of the image of D(h).

spans.label: cartesian square and transfer of openness

difficulty_reason: The criterion compresses universal openness of a ring-map spectrum into the openness of the image of a single principal open D(h) for h = sum x_i b_i in B[x_1,...,x_d]. The proof must run the reduction in the reverse direction: start from an arbitrary base change A -> A' and an arbitrary principal open D(g) in Spec(A' tensor_A B), rewrite g as sum a'_i tensor b_i, and then recognise a cartesian square of polynomial algebras in which the image of D(g) is exactly the inverse image of the given open. The step that is not a standard formality is that the chosen h must simultaneously encode every base change, which is why the proof needs the explicit polynomial presentation. Retained author proof at lines 21854-21875.
